transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Torres (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (NovaPay Eng Manager), Liam O'Connor (NovaPay SRE), Priya Rao (NovaPay ML Eng)

[00:00] Avery: okay hi everyone thanks for joining on time, this is our weekly throughput sync for the novapay pilot. quick check, any changes to attendees?
[00:07] Sara: all good, thanks.
[00:10] Miguel: hey all, i'll kick off with the numbers from last night's run, sorry the email had a tiny typo in the job id.
[00:17] Miguel: so we ran the 5k synthetic with continuous batching enabled, max_batch set to 64, concurrency 4. average tokens/sec per gpu was about 820 at p50 but p95 latency slipped to 420ms for long prompts.
[00:32] Priya: that p95 is a bit higher than we expected, our target is p95 < 300ms for the realtime route. are those long prompts including the 2k-context ones?
[00:40] Miguel: yeah we had a tail of requests with 1.2-1.6k tokens including system, so kv cache warmup was happening. prefix cache was hitting about 35% for repeated sessions.
[00:51] Liam: can you clarify "kv cache" - is that the model kv-store or your session cache? sometimes the naming in the logs is swapped.
[00:57] Miguel: good call - it's the model KV cache (we abbreviated as K V cache in the logs), so first full generation warms it and subsequent requests benefit. for intermittent traffic the warmup creates tail latency.
[01:10] Avery: quick context for folks: continuous batching tries to keep GPU pipelines full by grouping near-simultaneous requests; it's very sensitive to batch size and the inter-arrival distribution. lowering max_batch reduces p95 but hurts throughput and cost.
[01:26] Sara: from business side we care most about peak throughput during checkout spikes. cost is important but losing customers to latency is worse. we can accept slightly higher cost for the critical route.
[01:34] Priya: what about concurrency vs queueing - should we increase concurrency rather than large batches? we saw some worker saturation earlier when concurrency hit 12.
[01:42] Miguel: right, there's a tradeoff: more concurrency increases parallel in-flight requests but also increases memory pressure due to per-request kvs. on A100-like instances we saw safe concurrency up to 8 with our model and quantization profile. beyond that we start swapping or hitting oom.
[01:55] Priya: are you using int8 quantization for the model? that would change memory footprint.
[01:59] Miguel: yes we tested int8 and 4-bit quant, int8 gave us moderate memory savings, 4-bit saves more but increased slight output variance in a couple regen tests. we flagged that with your eval set last week.
[02:12] Sara: so what's the recommended config for the pci-real-time route?
[02:16] Avery: pragmatic recommendation: for real-time checkout route - set max_batch = 32, concurrency = 6, enable continuous batching with 20-30ms max latency window, and enable prefix caching for sessioned users. that should bring p95 closer to 280-320ms while keeping throughput decent.
[02:33] Liam: and for spike protection? we still need to avoid long queues that exceed our SLA.
[02:38] Miguel: add a soft queue size limit at the router (we recommend 250ms aggregated wait), and a hard cap that triggers fallback to a smaller model variant or to a cached response. Redwood has a fallback policy feature; we can wire it to return cached completions or route to hosted cheaper model.
[02:52] Sara: fallback to a smaller model for quality-sensitive flows sounds risky. can it return structured stub responses instead?
[02:58] Avery: yes that's a pattern we've seen: fallback returns a simplified structured reply or a cached canonical response for known prompts, or a short-form reply. we can demo that.
[03:07] Priya: on the numbers, can you share the cost delta between 32 vs 64 max_batch at our volume? we need ballpark per-1M tokens.
[03:13] Miguel: preliminary calc: with max_batch 64, you get ~12% lower cost per token because of batching efficiency; but because p95 increases we might lose conversions. with max_batch 32 cost goes up maybe 8% but latency improves. i'll produce a config diff and cost table.
[03:26] Liam: also curious on Dedicated vs Hosted: if we go Dedicated reservation, does continuous batching behave differently?
[03:32] Avery: dedicated gives you consistent GPU pools and you can tune instance types. continuous batching still works but with dedicated capacity the variance is lower and you can set higher concurrency safely because of guaranteed memory. downside is commit cost.
[03:44] Sara: security-wise we need SSO/SAML and audit logs - you told us Redwood Private can do VPC + KMS, is that right?
[03:51] Miguel: yes private deployment includes VPC peering options, KMS integration for encryption at rest, and audit trails. i will attach the SOC2/ISO summary and your sec pack after the call (there was a small typo in the filename last time, fixed).
[04:03] Priya: great. about the benchmark - can we run with a mixed prompt length distribution matching our traffic? i'll upload traces.
[04:10] Avery: that's crucial. please upload 72-hour traces with timestamps and we will re-run synthetic at 10k requests with that distribution. that will reveal batching behavior and tail latencies.
[04:20] Miguel: one more note on queueing: we saw that when inter-arrival spikes occur, the router's queue grows and continuous batching will enlarge batches which hurts latency; a hybrid approach with micro-batching for immediate requests and deferred batching for lower-priority requests helps.
[04:36] Sara: what's micro-batching vs continuous in practice?
[04:39] Miguel: micro-batching = very small max_batch (8-16) with short window (10-20ms) for critical route; continuous batching = larger window that coalesces more. hybrid sets critical routes to micro-batch and background jobs to continuous batching.
[04:54] Priya: okay makes sense. for the next run please also capture GPU utilization and memory per worker so we can tune concurrency.
[05:00] Miguel: will do, we'll include nvidia-smi style telemetry and our runtime counters (batch sizes, queue times, kv hit rate).
[05:08] Avery: i'll own the scheduling of the 10k benchmark and invite you to the run, and miguel will share the config diff.
[05:14] Liam: timeline check: we want to decide on prod model by mid-november, does that align?
[05:18] Sara: yes that's our internal timeline, need final numbers and cost estimates by the week of nov 15.
[05:24] Avery: noted. next steps recap - redwood runs benchmark, customer shares traces, redwood shares config and cost delta, schedule deep dive for queueing.
[05:33] Priya: quick question - any concerns with our VPC egress patterns? last time we saw some NAT gateway limits.
[05:38] Miguel: short answer: sounds like a platform issue on your side; Redwood's connectors are efficient but high egress can add latency; we can recommend private peering for production to remove NAT hops.
[05:48] Sara: okay please include the peering recommendation in the sec pack.
[05:52] Miguel: will do.
[05:55] Avery: anything else?
[05:57] Liam: no that's it for now. thanks everyone.
[06:00] Avery: thanks, we'll follow up with artifacts and invite.

[End of transcript]

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings ("K V cache" spacing), timestamps are approximate and every ~15-60s markers used.
